content.value: Primary reading: Rozanski and Woods, Chapters 8-10. Supplemental: SEI architecture evaluation material. This unit focuses on principles, constraints, and decisions.
Principles are durable design guidelines that help teams make consistent choices. They are useful only when they connect to real concerns and can be used to explain decisions.

A good decision record captures context, decision, status, consequences, and rationale. This lets future teams see why the architecture is the way it is, rather than reverse-engineering intent from code and diagrams.
Studio: write one architecture principle and one decision record for a system that must support offline mobile use.

concepts.name: Architecture principle
concepts.description: A durable design guideline used to make related architectural decisions consistent and explainable.

concepts.name: Decision record
concepts.description: A concise record of an architectural choice, its context, rationale, status, and consequences.

concepts.name: Decision consequence
concepts.description: An expected effect, tradeoff, obligation, or risk introduced by an architecture decision.

concepts.name: Principle traceability
concepts.description: The ability to connect architectural decisions back to stated principles and stakeholder concerns.
